newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW, Opel to resume car output after Spain strike.
newsitem.headline: VW, Opel to resume car output after Spain strike.

text.p: Two major German carmakers said on Thursday that they would soon resume vehicle production since the end of the Spanish truckers' strike will allow parts shipments to be resumed.
Adam Opel AG, a unit of General Motors Corp, said it would resume production at two German plants from Monday, while Volkswagen AG said it would resume some production of its Polo vehicle on Friday.
Opel said production of the Vectra saloon would resume on Monday at its plant in Ruesselsheim since parts deliveries from Spain would take a few days to reach the Frankfurt area plant.
At Opel's plant in Bochum, the spokesman said production would resume on Monday for the Astra vehicle.
It was still unclear when Opel would resume production of the Corsa vehicle at its Eisenach facility, the official said.
Opel had said on Tuesday that some 20,000 workers were affected by the suspension of production and that about 11,000 vehicles could not be built during the Spanish strike.
At Volkswagen, the carmaker said it would resume some production of the Polo vehicle on Friday and that it expected parts supplies to stabilise and for normal operations to resume on Monday.
Both carmakers have said work contracts would allow for additional shifts to make up for lost production.
